evals.prompt: Create a Python CLI tool called 'csvstats' that reads a CSV file and prints summary statistics for each numeric column (count, mean, median, min, max, standard deviation). It should handle missing values gracefully, support an optional --columns flag to select specific columns, and include proper error handling for malformed CSVs. Put it in a new 'tools/' directory with a sample CSV for testing.
evals.expected_output: A working Python CLI script with argument parsing, CSV reading, numeric column detection, stats calculation, --columns filtering, error handling, and a sample CSV file.

assertions.text: A csvstats.py file exists in the outputs
Script uses argparse or click for CLI argument parsing
A --columns flag is supported for selecting specific columns
All 6 statistics are calculated: count, mean, median, min, max, standard deviation
A sample CSV file is included for testing
Missing/empty values are handled without crashing
Non-existent file input produces a user-friendly error, not a raw traceback

evals.prompt: I have a bug in my project — there's no input validation anywhere. Add comprehensive input validation to any Python files in the codebase that accept user input or external data. Make sure edge cases are covered: empty strings, None values, type mismatches, boundary values. Add corresponding unit tests for each validation function.
evals.expected_output: Input validation added to relevant Python files with corresponding test files. Validation covers edge cases. Tests pass.

assertions.text: At least one Python file with validation functions exists
At least one test file exists
Validation covers empty string inputs
Validation covers None value inputs
Validation covers type mismatch inputs
Tests are runnable and pass when executed

evals.prompt: Create a simple but complete REST API rate limiter middleware in Python (using FastAPI or Flask, whichever makes more sense). It should support configurable rate limits per endpoint, use a sliding window algorithm, return proper 429 responses with Retry-After headers, and include both in-memory and Redis-backed storage options. Include tests.
evals.expected_output: Rate limiter middleware with sliding window, configurable per-endpoint limits, 429+Retry-After, dual storage backends, and tests.

assertions.text: Rate limiter middleware module exists
Sliding window algorithm is implemented (not fixed window or token bucket)
429 HTTP status code is returned when rate limit is exceeded
Retry-After header is included in 429 responses
In-memory storage backend is implemented
Redis storage backend is implemented
At least one test file exists
Per-endpoint rate limit configuration is supported
